method: Built by hand-checking public pages, 2026-09-26. Each state entry names the body that decides electric rates and large-load or data center tariffs, with its official site and the page where the public comments or searches dockets. Policy entries appear only where a real, dated rule, law or docket was found; docket and case numbers are copied as published by the commission, a legislature or the source named in the entry's summary (the Edison Electric Institute list of large-load tariffs, Sept. 2026, is the source where an entry says so, and its docket numbers were not independently re-checked on each commission's site). Proposal entries cover the five Florida proposals in frontend/src/data/florida_five.json plus 19 of the largest announced, paused, contested or approved campuses in backend/demo/datacenters_us.json; each status_note says 'as reported' and names its source, and unknown values are null. Nothing here implies wrongdoing, names an undisclosed tenant, or predicts an outage. Dates are YYYY-MM, or YYYY when only the year is published, or null when no date was found. Every URL returned HTTP 200 to a script, or is listed under verification: fetched with a different tool, or blocking automated requests (403, bot filter or unreachable from the build machine) but seen in search results. Extra optional keys: state 'note', decision_body 'how_to_comment'.

cases.title: Entergy Louisiana, ex parte: generation and transmission resources to serve a single customer in north Louisiana
cases.why: The commission approved the utility's plan for three gas plants and related transmission on Aug. 20, 2025 by a 4-1 vote (as reported); the docket remained open with follow-on filings.

meta-holly-ridge.status_note: As reported by KNOE and the Louisiana Illuminator, the commission voted 4-1 on Aug. 20, 2025 to approve Entergy Louisiana's application for gas plants and transmission to serve the campus in Richland Parish. The docket has stayed open with further proceedings.

decision_body.name: Hermantown City Council
decision_body.how_to_comment: Written comments go to the address listed on the city's project page, which also posts the environmental review documents, comment periods and meeting information.

cases.title: Minnesota Power: petition to approve an electric service agreement with Harmony Group, LLC for a Hermantown data center
cases.why: The commission decides whether the 15-year service agreement (about 700 MW of new wind and battery resources) is approved; Minnesota Power filed the petition March 27, 2026 and comments were accepted through July 21, 2026 (as reported). Search 26-159 in eDockets.

google-hermantown.status_note: Per the city's project page, the updated environmental review (AUAR) draft was open for comment June 11 to July 16, 2026, and the final was submitted Aug. 4, 2026; Google presented to the City Council and Planning and Zoning Commission Aug. 17-20 and gave a project update on Sept. 21, 2026. As reported by Northern News Now, a Sept. 8, 2026 council meeting was paused during heated public comment. The PUC docket is pending.

sources.title: City of Hermantown: Project page (environmental review, comment periods)
KAXE: More details emerge as Google, Hermantown work out data center agreements (May 20, 2026)
Minnesota Power petition to the PUC for the electric service agreement (March 26-27, 2026, PDF)
Northern News Now: Heated data center debate results in pause to Hermantown city council meeting (Sept. 9, 2026)

decision_body.name: Culpeper County Board of Supervisors
decision_body.how_to_comment: The board meets the first Tuesday of each month at 10 a.m. and 7 p.m. at 302 N. Main Street; agendas are in BoardDocs and you can email all members at BOS@culpepercounty.gov.

cases.title: Dominion Energy Virginia biennial review: new GS-5 rate class
cases.why: Dominion is the reported power source; its Nov. 25, 2025 order created a rate class for customers of 25 MW or more (75 percent load factor or higher) with minimum demand charges and long contracts, effective Jan. 1, 2027.

peterson-companies-culpeper.status_note: As reported by the Culpeper Times, the Board of Supervisors approved rezoning of a 34.4-acre parcel for the campus in 2023; an adjoining 115 acres had previously been rezoned by the Town of Culpeper. The developer says power would come from two Dominion Energy substations. No pending local vote was found as of the check date.

sources.title: InsideNoVa (Culpeper Times): McDevitt Drive rezoning request for data center approved (2023)
Peterson Companies: announces 2 million sq ft data center campus in Culpeper County (developer announcement)

decision_body.name: Coweta County Board of Commissioners
decision_body.how_to_comment: Agendas and minutes are in the county's CivicClerk portal (cowetacoga.portal.civicclerk.com).

prologis-newnan.status_note: As reported by the AJC and The Real Deal, the Board of Commissioners voted 3-2 in April 2026 to rezone about 830 acres from Rural Conservation to Industrial for the campus after 15 months of debate and a moratorium. Residents filed an appeal in Coweta County Superior Court on May 5, 2026 asking to reverse the rezoning (The Citizen; CBS Atlanta).

sources.title: AJC: $17B Project Sail data center project approved south of Atlanta (April 2026)
The Real Deal: Prologis wins approval for massive Georgia data center campus (April 10, 2026)

decision_body.name: Pima County Board of Supervisors
decision_body.how_to_comment: The county's Project Blue FAQ page summarizes the agreement and board actions.

cases.title: Tucson Electric Power: energy supply agreement with the Project Blue developer
cases.why: The commission approved the agreement on Dec. 3, 2025 by a 4-1 vote (as reported); on Feb. 19, 2026 the Arizona Attorney General appealed in Maricopa County Superior Court, arguing the rate-setting provision violates the Arizona Constitution (the Attorney General's release).

beale-infrastructure-tucson.status_note: As reported, the Pima County Board of Supervisors approved a community-benefit agreement 3-2 on Dec. 16, 2025 and the county's sale of the site closed Dec. 24, 2025. The Attorney General's appeal of the Corporation Commission approval is pending.

decision_body.name: Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection, Northwest Regional Office (air-quality and other permits)
decision_body.how_to_comment: DEP's Homer City page posts permit documents and the hearing record; a public hearing on the air permit was held Sept. 17, 2025.

homer-city-redevelopment-homer-city.status_note: Per DEP's page, the department issued a final plan approval (32-00457A) for the gas plant on Nov. 18, 2025 and renewed the Title V operating permit (32-00055) on Feb. 26, 2026; other mining, water, waste and waterway permitting processes remain active.

decision_body.name: Port Washington Common Council
decision_body.how_to_comment: The city's data center project page posts documents and updates.

cases.title: Wisconsin Electric Power Company (We Energies): Very Large Customer and Bespoke Resources tariffs
cases.why: We Energies' data center rate plan, approved in April 2026 with changes, sets how large data centers in its territory pay for power and grid costs (15-year minimum term, eligibility from 100 MW).

vantage-data-centers-port-washington.status_note: As reported by BizTimes, the Common Council unanimously approved a development agreement on Aug. 20, 2025 for the campus (about 1.3 GW on 672 acres). In August 2026 the Public Service Commission voted unanimously to make American Transmission Company restart its application for the transmission lines to serve the campus, restarting the 180-day review (Wisconsin Watch, Aug. 7, 2026).

decision_body.name: Mississippi Environmental Quality Permit Board (Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality)
decision_body.how_to_comment: MDEQ held a public hearing on the draft air permit on Feb. 17, 2026; permit decisions and appeal hearings are noticed on the MDEQ site.

xai-southaven.status_note: As reported by Mississippi Today, the Permit Board unanimously approved a construction permit for 41 gas-fired turbines at the site on March 10, 2026 after a public hearing where every speaker asked MDEQ to deny or delay it; residents and groups then petitioned MDEQ for a hearing to challenge the permit (April 2026).

decision_body.name: Independence City Council
decision_body.how_to_comment: The city's Nebius data center FAQ page answers common questions about the project.

nebius-independence.status_note: As reported by KCUR, the City Council voted 5-2 on March 2, 2026 to approve a Chapter 100 tax abatement for the project. Construction began in May 2026, and in July 2026 the city paused new data center applications, which does not affect this project (KCTV5, July 8, 2026).

sources.title: City of Independence: Nebius data center FAQs

decision_body.name: Van Wert City Council
decision_body.how_to_comment: Council meets at 6:30 p.m. on the second and fourth Mondays in Council Chambers at 515 East Main Street; agendas are posted on the city site.

cases.title: AEP Ohio data center tariff
cases.why: If served by AEP Ohio, new data centers above 25 MW pay for at least 85 percent of their contracted capacity under this approved tariff; the developer says it will fund the energy infrastructure the campus needs.

qts-data-centers-van-wert.status_note: As reported, Van Wert City Council annexed the site and rezoned it I-2 General Industrial shortly before the city and QTS announced, on May 29, 2026, a data center campus of roughly $10 billion (Lima Ohio; The VW Independent). The developer's announcement says it will pay for the energy infrastructure improvements and that there will be no cost impact to existing customers.

sources.title: City of Van Wert and QTS announce data center campus (QTS release, May 29, 2026)

decision_body.name: Millard County Commission
decision_body.how_to_comment: The commission meets in regular session at the Millard County Courthouse in Fillmore; agendas and minutes are on the county site, and the Planning Commission meets monthly in Delta.

creekstone-energy-delta.status_note: As reported by KSL (Nov. 2025), the Millard County Commission unanimously approved the zoning proposal and conditional use permit for the campus, which plans up to 10 GW over a decade from several power sources. An April 2026 company announcement (Utah Business) says the county also approved zoning for more than 1 GW of solar for the project.
